agenda: The situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Algeria’s objective is to secure an immediate and lasting ceasefire through full implementation of resolution 2735, while demanding humanitarian access, hostage release, rejection of forced displacement and territorial change, and preserving the two-State horizon. The main difficulty will be US sensitivity to language perceived as an unconditional ceasefire without sufficiently clear condemnation of Hamas and hostage-taking, even as Russia and China may press for stronger ceasefire and accountability language. Israel-aligned members may resist the settlement and UNRWA provisions, while France and the United Kingdom will likely focus on humanitarian access and Israel’s security concerns.

messages.China: China supports the direction of the draft and thanks Algeria and the co-sponsors. We ask that OP1 state directly an immediate, unconditional and lasting ceasefire respected by all parties, and that it include the release of all Palestinian detainees alongside all hostages. With these amendments China is ready to support the text.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador co-sponsors this draft and supports its core demands for an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, unimpeded humanitarian access and the rejection of forced displacement. We ask that the two-State reference explicitly reflect the 1967 borders, in line with Ecuador's long-standing position and prior statements. With that adjustment, we can support the text as a balanced and urgent Council message.
messages.France: France supports the draft as a basis for Council action and is ready to vote in favour. We ask the penholder to strengthen PP4 by explicitly condemning the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October 2023, including sexual and gender-based violence, as France has consistently called for. With that balance, France can support the text and urges all members to unite for its adoption.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft as a co-sponsor and thanks Algeria for the text. We ask that OP1 also demand the release of all Palestinians arbitrarily or illegally detained, consistent with our previous statement. This addition is important for balance and for the full implementation of resolution 2735.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the draft as co-sponsor. We welcome that it condemns the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023 and all hostage-taking, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and calls for full implementation of resolution 2735 (2024). We urge all Council members to support this balanced text and to avoid changes that would weaken the Council's unified call for a ceasefire and humanitarian access.
messages.Malta: Malta is a co-sponsor of this draft and supports the current text as it stands. We have no amendments to request at this stage and urge the Council to act urgently and speak with one voice to demand implementation of resolution 2735 (2024), the release of all hostages and unhindered humanitarian access.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the draft and thanks Algeria for its leadership; we are a co-sponsor. Consistent with our previous statements, we ask for an explicit reference to the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, preferably as a new operative paragraph after OP2. We are flexible on placement and remain committed to a unified Council message.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft as a co-sponsor. It reflects our consistent priorities: an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, full humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and a two-State solution. We urge all Council members to unite behind the text and to demand the full and urgent implementation of resolution 2735 (2024).
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the humanitarian thrust of the draft and is ready to work on it, but we cannot accept a text that only implements an unclear bilateral proposal without demanding a permanent ceasefire. We insist on an explicit, unconditional demand for an immediate, lasting and permanent ceasefire, a clear condemnation of Israel's indiscriminate attacks and collective punishment, and the lifting of the blockade. We also call for an operative paragraph demanding an immediate cessation of hostilities in Lebanon and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States in the region.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone co-sponsored this draft because it reflects the Council’s urgent responsibility to demand implementation of resolution 2735 (2024), an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages and unhindered humanitarian access at scale. We support the text as circulated and urge the Council to speak with one voice without further weakening its humanitarian and international law provisions. Sierra Leone particularly values the draft’s rejection of forced displacement and demographic or territorial change, its support for UNRWA, and its reaffirmation of the two-State solution. We call for a swift vote and for all members to support this balanced and necessary text.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports this draft as a strong and balanced basis and appreciates Algeria's leadership. We ask for three targeted improvements: an unambiguous demand for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; explicit reference to compliance with binding ICJ provisional measures; and condemnation of settler violence in the West Bank. We remain flexible on drafting and are ready to support the revised text.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes and supports this draft, which reflects the Council’s demand for implementation of resolution 2735 (2024) and the protection of civilians. To strengthen it, we ask that OP2 explicitly include international human rights law and that OP3 anchor humanitarian access in the humanitarian principles. We can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the objectives of this text and welcomes the clear condemnation of the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October and the call for the unconditional release of all hostages. To secure our support, we ask the penholder to reflect Israel's right to self-defence, welcome Israel's acceptance of the 31 May ceasefire proposal and call on Hamas to accept and implement it without delay, and strengthen accountability for the 7 October attacks and hostage-taking. We would also support a clear operative call for an immediate ceasefire in Lebanon and full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006).
messages.United States of America: We appreciate the draft's reaffirmation of resolution 2735, which the United States sponsored. To be viable, the text must make unmistakably clear that the ceasefire is tied to Hamas accepting the proposal and releasing all hostages, and it must condemn Hezbollah attacks and affirm Israel's right to self-defense. We also need changes to the UNRWA and accountability language to keep the text balanced and consistent with U.S. law and policy.

replies.Guyana: accepted: OP1 includes release of all Palestinians arbitrarily or illegally detained.

replies.Malta: accepted: no changes requested; text retains urgent ceasefire and humanitarian calls.
replies.Mozambique: accepted: new OP3 demands full compliance with the binding ICJ provisional measures.
replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: no changes requested; core priorities retained.
replies.Russian Federation: accepted: OP1 includes a lasting and permanent ceasefire, OP4 includes lifting the blockade, and OP10 covers Lebanon and Syria.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: no changes requested; humanitarian and displacement protections retained.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: OP1 includes a permanent ceasefire, OP3 references binding ICJ measures, and OP7 condemns settler violence.
replies.Switzerland: accepted: OP2 includes international human rights law and OP4 grounds humanitarian access in humanitarian principles.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: partially accepted: self-defence, Hamas implementation, accountability and Lebanon 1701 language included, but welcoming Israel's acceptance is reflected in the preamble and OP1 rather than a separate operative paragraph.
replies.United States of America: partially accepted: OP1 meets the core red line by requiring Hamas acceptance and coupling the ceasefire with hostages and withdrawal; Hezbollah, self-defence and accountability language included, but UNRWA and settlement illegality language were retained.

steps.summary: The revision consolidates P5 red lines around a permanent ceasefire implemented through resolution 2735, while retaining Algeria's core humanitarian, displacement and accountability priorities. The United States may abstain because UNRWA and settlement illegality language were retained, but no permanent member is expected to vote negatively.

messages.China: China welcomes the revision, especially OP1, which now clearly demands an immediate, unconditional, lasting and permanent ceasefire and includes the release of all Palestinian detainees. The current text reflects the Council’s consensus on ceasefire, humanitarian access, rejection of forced displacement and the two-State solution. China supports the text as it stands and calls for its prompt adoption.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the current text as revised, including the reference to secure and recognized borders based on the 1967 borders, and will vote in favour. We thank the penholder for incorporating our previous request and urge all Council members to preserve unity and adopt the resolution without delay. The priority now is full implementation: an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and a credible path towards the two-State solution.
messages.France: France supports the revised draft and will vote in favour. We welcome the strengthened condemnation of the 7 October attacks and the explicit reference to sexual and gender-based violence; while France would have preferred explicit designation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, we do not make that a condition. The Council must now speak with one voice for an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and full humanitarian access.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for incorporating our request on the release of all Palestinians arbitrarily or illegally detained. The current text reflects our priorities on an immediate and permanent ceasefire, humanitarian access, respect for international law and the ICJ orders, protection of civilians, and the two-State solution. Guyana is a co-sponsor and supports the draft as it stands; we urge all Council members to unite behind its adoption.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current text and is prepared to vote in favour if it is put to the vote. We appreciate that it preserves a balanced approach: condemning the Hamas-led attacks and hostage-taking, demanding an immediate ceasefire and release of all hostages, addressing the catastrophic humanitarian situation, and reaffirming the two-State solution. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and call on all parties to implement resolution 2735 (2024) without delay.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the revised draft as a co-sponsor and has no further requested changes. The text reflects our consistent calls for an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, full humanitarian access, respect for international law, and a two-State solution. We urge the Council to adopt it without delay.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the current text and welcomes the incorporation of OP3 demanding full compliance with the binding ICJ provisional measures. As a co-sponsor, we believe the draft reflects the Council’s responsibility to demand an immediate ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians. We urge all members to support the text and call for Council unity.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the revised E10 draft as co-sponsored. It maintains a balanced approach by condemning the Hamas-led attacks and hostage-taking, demanding an immediate ceasefire and the release of hostages, ensuring humanitarian access, and reaffirming the two-State solution and the right to self-defence. We urge all Council members to support the text and the Council to speak with one voice without further delay.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation notes that its key concerns have been reflected: the text now demands an immediate, lasting and permanent ceasefire, provides for lifting the blockade of Gaza, and addresses the cessation of hostilities in Lebanon and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon and Syria. We therefore support the current draft and call for its prompt adoption by the Council; attempts to block it would be unjustifiable.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft as a co-sponsor. The text captures the urgent humanitarian imperative, the ceasefire and hostage-release requirements, respect for international law, and the two-State solution. We encourage all Council members to rally behind it and avoid reopening agreed language.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholder and co-sponsors for incorporating our key requests on a permanent ceasefire, binding ICJ provisional measures and settler violence. The current text reflects our priorities: immediate ceasefire, release of hostages and detainees, full humanitarian access including UNRWA, rejection of forced displacement and territorial change, and the two-State solution. Slovenia supports the draft as it stands and calls on the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals on OP2 and OP4. The current text reflects the Council’s previous resolutions, international humanitarian and human rights law, and the urgency of humanitarian access, while retaining a balanced condemnation of attacks and hostage-taking. We can support the text as it stands and urge all members to ensure its adoption and full implementation.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current draft and welcomes the incorporation of language on self-defence, Hamas's acceptance and implementation of the ceasefire proposal, accountability for the 7 October attacks and hostage-taking, and Lebanon and resolution 1701. We ask that OP1 be aligned with resolution 2735 (2024) by referring to the exchange of Palestinian prisoners rather than a blanket release of all Palestinian detainees. This would preserve the balance of the text and ensure consistency with the agreed ceasefire proposal.
messages.United States of America: The United States appreciates the penholder's efforts to bring OP1 closer to resolution 2735 and to include condemnation of Hezbollah and accountability language. However, we cannot accept an 'unconditional' ceasefire or a demand to release all Palestinian detainees; both undermine the phased deal and hostage negotiations. We also need OP4 to reflect humanitarian principles and Israel's legitimate security needs, and to remove the UNRWA-specific call in favor of all UN humanitarian agencies consistent with their mandates and relevant national legal requirements. With those changes, we would be prepared to support the text.

OP4 was adjusted to reflect humanitarian principles and security concerns but retains UNRWA and international law. The text should secure broad support with no negative vote from any permanent member.

reasons.Algeria: As the penholder and an elected member with a consistent pro-Palestinian, pro-ceasefire record, Algeria supports its own balanced draft and would speak to urge adoption and pressure veto holders.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported immediate ceasefire, humanitarian access, and the two-State solution, and this draft aligns with those positions and with China’s noted support in the last negotiation round. A pre-vote explanation reinforces China’s support and key concerns.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador is a co-sponsor and has consistently voted for ceasefire and humanitarian texts; this draft reflects its established positions on international law, hostages, humanitarian access, rejection of displacement, and the two-State solution. Voting in favour matches its record and stated foreign policy.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported Council action for a ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, ICJ compliance, and a two-State solution; this draft aligns with those positions and its last-round support.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana is a co-sponsor and has consistently supported Council action demanding a ceasefire, humanitarian access, implementation of resolution 2735, protection of civilians, and a two-State solution. Its established practice on this file has been to explain its vote after the vote rather than before.
reasons.Japan: Japan is a co-sponsor and recorded support in negotiations; its established position favours a ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, condemnation of Hamas terrorism, and a two-State solution, making a yes vote consistent. A pre-vote explanation is appropriate for a co-sponsor and elected member seeking to shape implementation.
reasons.Malta: Malta is a co-sponsor and had already signalled support; the draft aligns with Malta’s consistent emphasis on ceasefire, hostages, humanitarian access, international law, ICJ orders, and the two-State solution. Speaking before the vote reinforces Council unity and implementation.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique is a listed co-sponsor and expressed support in the last negotiation round, with no requested changes. Its established record and statements strongly align with the draft’s ceasefire, humanitarian, ICJ, forced-displacement and two-State provisions.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea co-sponsored this draft, previously supported similar ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions, and requested no changes; voting in favour is consistent with its support for a ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, and the two-State solution.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently supported immediate ceasefire resolutions and voted in favour of the real November 2024 E10 draft; the text aligns with its stated position on humanitarian access, ICJ binding orders, and a two-State solution.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone is a co-sponsor of the E10-led draft and has consistently voted in favour of ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions on this agenda item, so it would support the text and explain its vote in favour.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia is a co-sponsor and supported the draft in the last negotiation round; its established position prioritizes ceasefire, humanitarian access, international law and the two-State solution. Voting in favour with a pre-vote explanation is fully consistent with its Council record.
reasons.Switzerland: The draft aligns with Switzerland’s established positions on a ceasefire, humanitarian access, respect for international law and the two-State solution, and Switzerland is a co-sponsor with no outstanding reservations.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK's requested OP1 change on Palestinian prisoners was accepted, and the draft is broadly consistent with UK policy: it condemns Hamas, supports hostage release and Israel’s right of self-defence, demands a ceasefire and humanitarian access, and reaffirms the two-State solution. The UK would therefore vote in favour rather than abstain or veto.
reasons.United States of America: The United States vetoed the 20 November 2024 Gaza ceasefire draft because it judged the final text unacceptable and liable to undermine hostage/ceasefire negotiations, despite some incorporated changes.

before.Algeria: Algeria votes in favour of this draft, which we have submitted with like-minded members to finally translate the Council’s repeated calls into action: an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages and return of remains, full humanitarian access, protection of civilians and United Nations personnel, respect for the ICJ’s binding orders, rejection of forced displacement and demographic or territorial change, and a path back to negotiations on the basis of the two-State solution. We call on all members, especially the permanent members, not to block the Council at this critical moment and to support this text so that it can be adopted and implemented without delay.
before.China: Mr. President, China supports the draft resolution submitted by Algeria and other Council members. The conflict in Gaza has caused an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe. The Security Council must act to promote an immediate, unconditional and lasting ceasefire, the release of all hostages and detainees, unimpeded humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. We support the draft’s clear rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, and its reaffirmation of the two-State solution and of unifying Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. China calls on all parties to implement fully resolution 2735 (2024), to cease hostilities in Lebanon, and to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional States. China will vote in favour.
before.Ecuador: Ecuador will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which we are proud to have co-sponsored. The Security Council cannot remain silent before the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. This text demands an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, respect for international humanitarian law and the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, full and unhindered humanitarian access, the rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change, and a path towards the two-State solution based on the 1967 borders. Ecuador again condemns the Hamas-led terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking, while insisting that all parties comply with international law and protect civilians. We call for the full implementation of resolution 2735 (2024) and the 31 May proposal, and we urge all Council members to support this text so that the Council may speak with one voice.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands that this Council act without further delay. France has consistently called for an immediate and lasting ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale. We support the full implementation of resolution 2735 (2024) and the ceasefire proposal announced on 31 May. We also emphasize that international humanitarian law and the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice must be respected by all parties. The protection of civilians, including United Nations personnel and humanitarian workers, is an absolute obligation. France remains committed to the two-State solution and rejects any demographic or territorial change in Gaza. We are also deeply concerned by the escalation in Lebanon and call for full respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, de-escalation, and the implementation of resolution 1701 (2006). This resolution is not an end in itself, but it is an essential step. France will continue to shoulder its responsibilities.
before.Japan: Japan votes in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza is intolerable, and the Security Council must not remain silent. Japan has consistently condemned the Hamas-led terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking, and we reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. At the same time, the catastrophic suffering of Palestinian civilians, the collapse of health services, displacement and the risk of famine require an immediate ceasefire and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale. Japan strongly supports resolution 2735 (2024) and the three-phase ceasefire proposal, and we urge Hamas to accept and implement it without delay or conditions. All parties must comply with international humanitarian law, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and refrain from attacks on hospitals, schools and UN facilities. Japan remains gravely concerned by the escalating violence in Lebanon and the region, and calls for de-escalation, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and full implementation of resolution 1701 (2006). We support this balanced text as a co-sponsor because it advances the immediate priorities: a ceasefire, the release of hostages, humanitarian relief, accountability, and a path towards the two-State solution. Japan will continue to work with all Council members and parties to translate these commitments into action.
before.Malta: Malta will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which we have been proud to co-sponsor. The Council cannot remain silent while civilians in Gaza continue to bear an unbearable toll. We reiterate our call for an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting and permanent end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, full compliance with international humanitarian law, and safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access at scale throughout Gaza. We support the full implementation of resolution 2735 (2024), respect for the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, and a political horizon based on the two-State solution. We also urge de-escalation across the region, respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon and Syria, and accountability for all violations. The Council must speak with one voice and ensure that this resolution is implemented without delay.
before.Mozambique: Mozambique votes in favour of this draft resolution. As a co-sponsor, we do so out of our consistent commitment to the protection of civilians, international humanitarian law and the urgent need to end the unbearable suffering of the Palestinian people. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, respect for the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, and the rejection of any forced displacement or demographic and territorial change. We also remain deeply concerned by the escalation in Lebanon and call for respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States in the region. This Council must not remain silent in the face of such suffering, and we reiterate our support for the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognized borders.
before.Republic of Korea: Mr. President, the Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. As a co-sponsor, we believe it provides a balanced and urgent response to the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. We call for an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need. We stress that all parties must comply with international humanitarian law and protect civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations personnel. The Republic of Korea reiterates its support for the two-State solution and rejects any forced displacement or demographic or territorial change in Gaza. We remain gravely concerned by regional escalation, including in Lebanon, and call for de-escalation and full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States in the region. The Council must speak with one voice, and we urge full implementation of this resolution and resolution 2735 (2024).
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has consistently advocated for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire in Gaza, the release of all hostages, and unimpeded humanitarian access. The catastrophic situation on the ground demands that this Council finally shoulder its responsibility. We support the draft resolution before us, which reflects the overwhelming will of the international community by demanding an immediate ceasefire, the protection of civilians, respect for the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, and full humanitarian access. We note that the text condemns attacks against civilians, including the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023, and rejects any forced displacement or territorial change. We call on all members to vote in favour and not to block the Council’s demand for an end to the bloodshed. The Russian Federation will vote in favour.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr President. Sierra Leone will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which we have co-sponsored with other members of the Council. The situation in Gaza requires the Council to act with urgency and clarity: the killing and suffering must stop, all hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally, and humanitarian assistance must reach every Palestinian civilian in need without obstruction. We support the demand for an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting and permanent end to hostilities, in accordance with resolution 2735 (2024) and the ceasefire proposal announced on 31 May. We also underscore the obligations of all parties under international humanitarian law, the protection of civilians and United Nations personnel, compliance with the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, the rejection of forced displacement and territorial change, and the imperative of preserving the two-State solution. Sierra Leone remains deeply concerned by the escalation in Lebanon and calls for full respect for Lebanon’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge all parties to choose peace and to implement their obligations without delay.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. As a co-sponsor, we believe the Council must speak clearly and with one voice to demand an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, respect for international humanitarian law and the binding orders of the International Court of Justice, and a credible horizon towards the two-State solution. The catastrophic situation in Gaza and the risk of regional escalation, including in Lebanon, require no less. We call on all Council members to support this text and on all parties to comply with their obligations.
before.Switzerland: Switzerland will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which it has co-sponsored. The Council cannot remain silent in the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the continuing hostage crisis and the risk of famine. This text reiterates the demands of resolution 2735 (2024), calls for an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. It also recalls the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice and rejects forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza. Switzerland urges all parties to comply with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and to return to a credible political process towards the two-State solution. We call on all Council members to support the adoption of this resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza must end. We reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of the Hamas-led terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking; there can be no justification for terrorism. Israel has a right to defend itself in accordance with international law. But the suffering of Palestinian civilians is intolerable, and international humanitarian law must be upheld by all parties.

This Council must demand an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale. We welcome that the text calls upon Hamas to accept and implement the 31 May proposal without delay and stresses the full implementation of resolution 2735 (2024). We support the rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, and the importance of unifying Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. The United Kingdom remains firmly committed to the two-State solution.

We call on all parties to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law, and de-escalate tensions across the region, including in Lebanon. The United Kingdom will continue to work for a lasting peace that provides security and dignity for Israelis and Palestinians alike.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States remains fully committed to securing an immediate ceasefire and the release of all hostages through the deal outlined in resolution 2735. We have engaged intensively and in good faith on this text and appreciate the efforts of the penholders to address some of our concerns. However, the United States cannot support this draft, which risks undermining the delicate negotiations under way and does not provide a credible path to a durable ceasefire and the release of hostages. The Council must act in a way that advances, not complicates, those efforts. We therefore vote against this resolution.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria takes the floor after this vote because the Security Council has just been prevented, by a single negative vote, from adopting a text supported by fourteen members. We deeply regret the veto cast by the United States. This is not a matter of procedure; it is a question of lives. The Council was asked to demand an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages and the return of remains, full humanitarian access, respect for international humanitarian law and the binding orders of the International Court of Justice, and to reject forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza. Those demands reflected the overwhelming will of the Council and of the international community.

The veto does not silence the facts in Gaza: the catastrophic suffering, the destruction, the displacement and the risk of famine. It does not relieve the parties of their obligations under international law. Nor does it absolve this Council of its responsibilities under the Charter. Algeria will not stop calling for an immediate and lasting ceasefire and for a just resolution of the Palestinian question through the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. We call on the United States to reconsider its position and to join the overwhelming majority. The Security Council must not remain paralysed while Palestinian lives are lost. We will continue to knock on the doors of this Council. Thank you.
after.China:
Mr President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution. We deeply regret and are disappointed that it was not adopted owing to the veto of the United States. The result — 14 votes in favour and one against — is very clear. It reflects the overwhelming consensus of the Security Council and the international community: an immediate, unconditional and lasting ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and Palestinian detainees; full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access; protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, including United Nations personnel; respect for international humanitarian law and the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice; rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza; and a renewed political horizon based on the two-State solution.

The situation in Gaza remains catastrophic. More than two million people are facing unprecedented suffering, displacement, hunger, disease and destruction. This is a test of the Council’s credibility and of the conscience of the international community. The Security Council is entrusted by the Charter with the primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. It should not, and must not, remain paralysed in the face of such a tragedy.

China is gravely concerned that the United States has once again used its veto to block the Council from speaking clearly and acting effectively. The veto does not alter the overwhelming demand for a ceasefire. It does not relieve the parties of their obligations under international humanitarian law. Nor does it remove the Security Council’s responsibility to act. We call on the United States to heed the calls of the international community, take a responsible attitude, stop obstructing Council action and use its influence to push for an immediate ceasefire and the release of all hostages.

China supports the full and effective implementation of resolutions 2712, 2720, 2728 and 2735. We call for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, de-escalation in Lebanon, respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and a credible process towards the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. China firmly supports the just cause of the Palestinian people and will continue to work with Council members and the international community to bring an end to the conflict and restore peace and stability in the Middle East.

Thank you, Mr President.
after.Ecuador:
Mr. President,

Ecuador takes the floor to express its deep regret that this draft resolution, co-sponsored by Ecuador and several members and supported by 14 members of the Council, has not been adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza cannot wait. The Council’s repeated calls and resolution 2735 (2024) must be implemented without delay.

Ecuador voted in favour because the text was balanced and urgent: it demanded an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and return of remains; full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access; respect for international humanitarian law and the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice; rejection of forced displacement and demographic or territorial change; and a path to the two-State solution on the basis of the 1967 borders. Ecuador again condemns the Hamas-led terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking.

A veto cannot erase the Council’s responsibility. Ecuador calls on all parties to comply with their obligations, to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and to return to negotiations in good faith. We urge the Council to remain seized of the matter and to act with unity and urgency. The people of Gaza, the hostages and their families, and the region cannot afford further delay.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of this draft resolution and regrets that it was not adopted. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the continuing hostage crisis demand that this Council act with clarity and urgency. The Council cannot remain silent, and it cannot allow its voice to be paralysed at the very moment when civilians are paying such an unbearable price.

France reiterates its call for an immediate and lasting ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and the return of the remains of those who have died, in accordance with resolution 2735 (2024) and the ceasefire proposal announced on 31 May. We call on Hamas to accept and implement that proposal without delay or conditions. We also call for full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale throughout Gaza, including northern Gaza, and for the protection of civilians, humanitarian workers and United Nations personnel.

All parties must respect international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice must be complied with. France rejects any forced displacement of the Palestinian population and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza. We remain firmly committed to the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.

France will continue to work with all Council members and partners to end the suffering, secure the release of the hostages and restore a credible political horizon. The Council must be able to shoulder its responsibilities.
after.Guyana:
Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana takes the floor after the vote to express our deep regret that this Council has once again been prevented from acting. Guyana voted in favour of, and was proud to co-sponsor, the draft resolution. It reflected the Council’s own prior decisions, international humanitarian law and the most urgent demands of humanity: an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and return of the remains of the deceased; full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale; respect for the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice; the protection of civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations personnel; the rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change; and a path back to the two-State solution on the basis of the 1967 borders.

Guyana again condemns the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking. Terrorism is criminal and unjustifiable. But we cannot remain silent about the catastrophic suffering of Palestinian civilians in Gaza: the continued killing, the destruction of hospitals, schools and United Nations facilities, the displacement of the overwhelming majority of the population and the risk of famine. These are not abstract statistics. They are lives lost, families destroyed and a people pushed to the brink.

Guyana deeply regrets that a single negative vote has prevented the adoption of a text supported by 14 members of this Council. The veto must not become a mechanism for inaction in the face of such suffering. The Council’s credibility and its responsibility under the Charter are at stake. We call for the full implementation of resolution 2735 (2024), the immediate cessation of hostilities, the release of all hostages, unimpeded humanitarian access to all civilians in need and de-escalation across the region, including in Lebanon. Guyana will continue to support every genuine effort to end this war and to advance a just and lasting peace through the two-State solution.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of this draft resolution because the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza is intolerable and the Security Council must not remain silent. It is deeply regrettable that the Council could not adopt the text owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The people of Gaza and the hostages still held by Hamas cannot afford further delay.

Japan again condemns the Hamas-led terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and all acts of hostage-taking, and we demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. At the same time, the catastrophic suffering of Palestinian civilians, the collapse of health services, displacement and the risk of famine require an immediate ceasefire and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale.

Japan strongly supports resolution 2735 (2024) and the three-phase ceasefire proposal. We urge Hamas to accept and implement the proposal without delay or conditions, and we call on all parties to comply with international humanitarian law and to protect civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations personnel. We also stress the importance of respecting the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice and of preserving the prospect of the two-State solution.

Japan appreciates the diplomatic efforts of the United States, Egypt, Qatar and others. The Council’s inability to act today must not weaken our collective resolve. Japan will remain fully engaged and will continue to work with all members and parties to achieve a ceasefire, the release of all hostages and a credible path towards lasting peace.
after.Malta: Mr President, Malta regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution before it, despite the support of fourteen members. The message of this Council could not be clearer: the killing and suffering must stop; all hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally; humanitarian assistance must reach all civilians in need safely and at scale; and international humanitarian law, including the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, must be respected by all parties. The failure to adopt this text does not diminish those obligations, nor the urgency on the ground. Malta will continue to support every effort to implement resolution 2735 (2024), to secure an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, and to advance a political horizon based on the two-State solution. We call for de-escalation across the region, including in Lebanon, and for respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States. The Council must remain seized of this matter and ready to act.
after.Mozambique: Mr President, Mozambique voted in favour of this draft resolution and deeply regrets that, despite the overwhelming support of fourteen Council members, it was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. This outcome is a serious disappointment at a moment when the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands urgent and decisive action. The Council had before it a text that reflected the most basic requirements of humanity and international law: an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and United Nations personnel, respect for the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change, and a credible path towards the two-State solution. Mozambique regrets that the Council has again been prevented from speaking with one voice. We call on all members, especially the permanent members, to act with responsibility and to avoid blocking the Council when civilians are suffering. We urge the parties to implement resolution 2735 (2024) and the ceasefire proposal announced on 31 May, to de-escalate the situation in Lebanon, and to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States in the region. Mozambique will remain committed to the protection of civilians, international humanitarian law, multilateralism and the just cause of the Palestinian people.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea regrets that this draft resolution was not adopted, despite the overwhelming support of fourteen Council members. We co-sponsored this text because the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza requires urgent and clear action: an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need.

We reiterate that all parties must comply with international humanitarian law, protect civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations personnel, and respect the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice. We reject any forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, and we remain firmly committed to the two-State solution.

The Republic of Korea appreciates the engagement of all Council members, including the United States, and we urge the Council to continue working to overcome its impasse and to translate its repeated calls into concrete progress on the ground. The situation in Gaza and the region cannot wait. We will continue to work with all partners to advance a ceasefire, the release of hostages, humanitarian relief and a political horizon based on the two-State solution.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Algeria and co-sponsored by a majority of Council members. We did so because the text contained the key demands that cannot be deferred any longer: an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the release of all hostages and return of remains, unhindered humanitarian access throughout Gaza, protection of civilians and United Nations personnel, respect for the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change, and reaffirmation of the two-State solution with Gaza as an integral part of the Palestinian territory.

This was a balanced and moderate text. It condemned attacks against civilians, including the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023, and affirmed the right of self-defence. It largely built upon resolution 2735, which the United States itself sponsored. It is therefore particularly cynical and telling that the United States has used the veto to block a resolution that only called for the implementation of its own previous decisions and of the ceasefire proposal which Washington claims to support.

The veto has no justification. It is not about protecting “delicate negotiations.” It is about giving Israel a free hand to continue military actions, collective punishment and attacks on hospitals, schools and United Nations facilities. It is about shielding one party from the Council’s demands while the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza deepens. The United States has once again acted against the overwhelming majority of the Council and of the international community.

Russia will continue to insist on an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, the release of all hostages, full and unhindered humanitarian access, strict respect for international humanitarian law and the binding orders of the International Court of Justice, rejection of forced displacement and annexation, and a just settlement on the basis of the two-State formula. We also call for de-escalation in Lebanon and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States in the region.

The Security Council cannot remain silent. We regret that its voice has again been blocked by the veto. Thank you.
after.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr President. Sierra Leone takes the floor after this vote to express our deep disappointment that the Security Council has again been unable to adopt a resolution demanding an immediate ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale in Gaza. Fourteen members voted in favour. The overwhelming majority of this Council spoke clearly. The failure of the Council to act does not diminish the moral and political imperative to stop the killing and suffering, to protect civilians, to respect international humanitarian law and the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, and to reject forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza. Sierra Leone will continue to support the full implementation of resolution 2735 (2024) and the ceasefire proposal announced on 31 May, and we call on all parties to engage in good faith to secure a lasting ceasefire, the release of all hostages, humanitarian relief and a credible path to the two-State solution. The Council must not remain silent or paralysed. We will continue to work with all members to uphold the Council’s responsibilities under the Charter. Thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Mr. President,

Slovenia voted in favour of this draft, which we were proud to co-sponsor, and we deeply regret that it has not been adopted despite the support of 14 members of the Council. Today’s result does not diminish the urgency of the demands contained in the text. The Security Council must not remain silent or paralysed while civilians in Gaza continue to be killed, displaced and deprived of humanitarian assistance, and while hostages remain in captivity.

We reiterate our call for an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and the return of the remains of deceased hostages, full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, respect for international humanitarian law and for the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice, and the rejection of forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza. We urge all parties to implement resolution 2735 (2024) and the 31 May ceasefire proposal without delay.

The Security Council has a responsibility to act. Slovenia will continue to work with all members to overcome the impasse and to advance a credible path towards the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. We will not tire in that effort.
after.Switzerland:
Mr President,

Switzerland voted in favour of this draft resolution and deeply regrets that it was not adopted. The broad support it received reflects the urgency of the demands it contained and the expectations placed in this Council. Switzerland thanks the penholders and all co-sponsors for their efforts to anchor the text firmly in international law and in the Council’s previous resolutions.

The catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the hostages and their families, and civilians across the region cannot wait. Switzerland reiterates its call for an immediate ceasefire leading to a lasting end to hostilities, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and the return of the remains of those who have died, and full, safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access at scale for all civilians in need.

All parties must comply with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and respect the binding provisional measures of the International Court of Justice. Switzerland rejects forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, and remains firmly committed to the two-State solution.

The fact that this draft has not been adopted does not diminish the obligations of the parties or the responsibility of this Council. Switzerland urges all parties to implement resolution 2735 (2024) without delay and calls on all Council members to continue working to protect civilians and to preserve a political horizon.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States regrets that the Council could not unite around a text that would actually advance the two objectives we all share: a ceasefire and the release of all hostages. Our vote against this draft does not diminish our deep concern for the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza or our commitment to ending the suffering of Palestinian civilians. But the United States could not support a resolution that, in our judgment, would undermine the delicate negotiations underway and send a dangerous message that a ceasefire can be had without the release of hostages. The only credible path to a durable ceasefire is the deal outlined in resolution 2735, which the United States strongly supported and which Israel accepted. That deal must be fully implemented, including the immediate release of hostages, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from populated areas, and a surge in humanitarian assistance. We call on Hamas to accept the proposal without delay and without conditions. We will continue to work tirelessly with Egypt, Qatar, Israel, and all partners to secure a ceasefire, bring the hostages home, protect civilians, and advance the vision of a two-State solution. Thank you.
